situation.note: 12 hour night shifts, I send half my salary home, my parents are proud but every call ends with when are you getting married. I'm 31 and I feel like I'm failing at a test I never agreed to take

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call needing their approval, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: By the end of the week the test you feel you are failing is named, and the part of you that can stand in its own worth has the floor.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the pride and the question, and the restless mind between them, named without blame.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the restless mind comes from needing their approval to settle a clock that is not yours.
week_beats.steady: You hold that praise and blame come and go, and what is yours to do is yours to do.
week_beats.act: You try being on your own side for one evening, letting their praise and their questions come and go without deciding your worth.

understanding.core_struggle: A woman working -hour night shifts and sending money home feels she is failing a test she never agreed to take, because every call ends with when are you getting married.
understanding.mirror: You send them half your salary, and every call ends with the same question you never asked.
understanding.insight: You are building something for them with your work, and the test you feel you are failing is the one they keep asking about.

queries.hook: The pride in their voice and the question at the end of every call, and the restless mind that cannot settle between the two. My parents' expectations weigh on me.
queries.diagnose: When your worth depends on their approval, every word of blame or pressure shakes you; craving approval keeps the mind unsteady.
queries.steady: Praise and blame come and go like the wind; what is yours to do is yours to do, and no one else can take that from you.
queries.act: Practise being on your own side; let their praise and their questions come and go without letting either decide your worth today.
queries.story: A woman who built something for her family with her own hands, faced the same question again and again, and found a way to stand in her own worth.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

matched.label: I can't focus, my mind is restless
I feel anxious most of the time

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is restless and stubborn, like the wind, and impossible to hold. Krishna agrees it is hard to control, but he says that practice and letting go can train it. The mind feels like a force of nature, but it can be shaped by steady effort.
verse.for_you: You are carrying the weight of their pride and the marriage question, and your mind is restless between them. Let the wanting be seen, and let your focus stay on the work.
verse.try_today: Notice when the mind drifts to their question, and let it go without answering it.
verse.scene_line: You are in the middle of the shift, holding the phone call and the work at once.
asks: How do I hold the pride and the question at the same time?

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: From the section on wealth: how the world treats someone who has lost money.
verse.sanskrit: तानीन्द्रियाण्यविकलानि तदेव नाम सा बुद्धिरप्रतिहता वचनं तदेव । अर्थोष्मणा विरहितः पुरुषः क्षणेन सोऽप्यन्य एव भवतीति विचित्रमेतत् ॥
verse.line: Same person, same mind, same voice. Lose money, and people suddenly treat you as someone else.
verse.translation: The same faculties, unimpaired; the same name; the same unclouded mind; the same speech. Yet a man deprived of the warmth of wealth becomes, in a moment, someone else. How strange!
verse.why: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.
verse.misuse: The verse mocks how the world sees you; it does not measure your worth.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On wealth
prasang.summary: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.
prasang.lesson: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to you from the section on wealth. He looks at a man who still has the same mind, the same voice, the same unclouded faculties, but has just lost his money. The world suddenly treats him as someone else. Bhartrihari asks how strange this is. The verse proposes that money changes how others see you, not who you are. It is a wry look at how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value.
verse.for_you: You are working the night shift, sending half your pay home, and your parents still end every call with the same question about marriage.
verse.try_today: Notice when the mind starts to settle their clock instead of yours.
verse.scene_line: You are the same person on the phone, yet the world has changed who they see.
asks: What part of me is the same person even when the calls end?
How do I live in a world that only sees the salary?

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks from a place of having seen how quickly the world shifts. The same people who praise you today will treat you differently if your money vanishes tomorrow. He is not saying to ignore them. He is saying the steady person does not let the crowd decide their path. The path is already there. The praise and the blame are just weather. They come and they go, but the work stays. The steadfast person keeps moving forward on what is right, because the path itself does not depend on what anyone says.
verse.for_you: You send money home and they praise you, then they ask when you will marry. The praise and the pressure are the same noise. You can let the noise move around you. Your part is the work, the shift, the sending. That is the path.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when the phone call ends and their voice fades, and feel the path still under your feet.
verse.scene_line: You are the struck ball, still bouncing on the path they cannot see.
asks: How do I stop the phone call from ending in marriage?
Can I let the blame go without letting them down?

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: न हृष्यत्यात्मसंमाने नावमानेन तप्यते / गाङ्गो ह्रद इवाक्षोभ्यो यः स पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Don't swell with praise or burn at a slight; stay deep and still like a river pool.
verse.translation: One who is not elated when honoured, nor pained when slighted, and who stays unruffled like a deep pool of the Ganga, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

verse.for_you: Every call with your parents ends with the same question about marriage, and that is a slight that burns. But your work is yours to do. Let the praise and the pressure come and go, and stay deep and still like a river pool. You are not failing the test.
verse.try_today: When the next call ends with their question, let it pass without answering.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own night, waiting before the talks, and the counsel is to stay deep and still.
asks: How do I stay deep when the water is always stirred?
Can I forgive the question without forgiving the pressure?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna is frozen in doubt. Krishna tells him that the self can be its own best friend or its own worst enemy. The self alone lifts itself up by itself and does not let itself sink. The choice is whether to be your own enemy by doubting and sinking, or your own friend by lifting up.
verse.for_you: You are on the night shift, sending half your pay home, and your parents end every call with a question about marriage. Their praise feels good, but their questions make you feel like you are failing a test you never agreed to take.
verse.try_today: When the phone rings at home, let their words come and go without deciding your worth.
verse.scene_line: You are on the night shift, and the phone rings at home.
asks: What does it mean to be my own friend when my family is right there?
How do I lift myself up when I feel like I am failing?

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on inner stillness in an active life.
verse.sanskrit: बहिःकृत्रिमसंरंभो हृदि संरम्भवर्जितः । कर्ता बहिरकर्तान्तर्लोके विहर शुद्धधीः ॥
verse.line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
verse.translation: Outwardly busy, inwardly free of agitation; a doer on the outside, a non-doer within: move through the world with a clear mind.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha how a person who is free inside lives in the world. He says they should let things go that are lost, take up what comes next, do the work in front of them, and speak gently. They can be busy on the outside, but inside they stay free from agitation. They move through the world with a clear mind, doing what is needed without letting it shake them.
verse.for_you: The same mind that sends half your salary home and works the night shift can also hold your worth without needing their call to end in marriage. Let their questions come and go like the work itself. You are the one doing the work, and that is enough.
verse.try_today: Let their praise and their questions come and go without deciding your worth for one evening.
verse.scene_line: You are busy on the outside and unhurried inside, letting their questions come and go.
asks: How do I let their questions come and go without deciding my worth?
How do I stay unhurried inside when their calls weigh on me?

story.title: Parvati holds to her choice
story.story_hook: The sages came to talk Parvati out of it, and they listed every flaw in the man she had chosen.
story.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
story.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

anchor.speaker: Parvati
anchor.setting: Parvati answers the sages who mock her resolve to win Shiva through years of austerity.
anchor.sanskrit: सत्य कहेहु गिरिभव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटै बरु देहा॥ कनकउ पुनि पषान तें होई। जारेहुँ सहजु न परिहर सोई ॥
anchor.line: Gold comes from stone, and even in fire it stays gold. Hold to what you are.
anchor.translation: You speak truly: this body was born of a mountain, so its resolve will not break, even if the body does. Gold too is born of stone, and even in fire it does not give up its nature.
anchor.why: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.
anchor.misuse: Steadiness is not stubbornness; keep checking that the goal is still worth it.

prasang.title: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
prasang.story_hook: The sages came to talk Parvati out of it, and they listed every flaw in the man she had chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

story.hook_title: The sages listed every flaw in the man Parvati had chosen
story.teaser: The sages listed every flaw in the man Parvati had chosen
story.for_you: Parvati heard every reason to change her mind and she did not. You are hearing the same list every night. Choose once more, in silence, that this path is yours. Gold stays gold in the fire.
asks: How do I hold to my own choice when the phone never stops ringing?
What if the path I chose is the one that makes them proudest?
Where does the test end and my own life begin?
